title: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability
An optimum character recognition system using decision functions
abstract: Formulates recognition with an explicit reject option using statistical decision theory. It characterizes optimal decisions either by expected risk or by minimizing error for a specified rejection rate, providing foundational machinery for cost-sensitive abstention.

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
abstract: Characterizes pattern-recognition performance through the joint error-reject tradeoff and derives an optimum rejection rule. The work provides foundational theory for evaluating selective systems by considering error and useful coverage together.

title: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method
abstract: Introduces the Pyramid Method for evaluating summary content using semantic content units derived from multiple human summaries. The method weights facts by their frequency across references, providing an explicit notion of important-content coverage rather than relying only on surface overlap.

title: Overview of the TAC 2008 Update Summarization Task
abstract: Describes the TAC update-summarization evaluation in which systems summarize a later document set under the assumption that a reader has already seen an earlier set. Human evaluation covers content, readability, and overall responsiveness, with content assessed using the Pyramid method, making the task relevant to evaluating omission and novelty under temporal updates.

title: Summarization of changes in dynamic text collections using Latent Dirichlet Allocation model
abstract: Studies summarization of significant changes in evolving document collections rather than summarization of a static snapshot. It evaluates methods on Wikipedia revision histories and explicitly models information changes occurring during specified temporal intervals.

title: Overview of the TREC 2016 Real-Time Summarization Track
abstract: Presents an evaluation track for continuously monitoring document streams and delivering timely, novel information for persistent user interests. The setting directly exposes evaluation issues around evolving information, prior-reader state, timeliness, novelty, and useful coverage.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classification for deep neural networks, allowing a user to specify a desired risk level while the system rejects enough predictions to meet that risk with high probability. Evaluation explicitly couples risk and coverage, making it a foundational transfer result for calibrated abstention.

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
abstract: Introduces an end-to-end neural architecture that jointly optimizes prediction and rejection rather than thresholding a separately trained classifier. Experiments evaluate the resulting risk-coverage tradeoff on classification and regression tasks.

title: Towards Improving Selective Prediction Ability of NLP Systems
abstract: Studies selective prediction in NLP under both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions. It trains a calibrator using model confidence and instance difficulty to predict correctness and evaluates whether abstention can improve reliability under distribution shift.

title: EmailSum: Abstractive Email Thread Summarization
abstract: Introduces an abstractive email-thread summarization dataset with short and long human summaries and evaluates multiple summarization approaches. Human evaluation reveals challenges involving sender intent and participant roles, while standard automatic metrics correlate weakly with human judgments.

title: QuestEval: Summarization Asks for Fact-based Evaluation
abstract: Proposes a question-answering-based summarization metric intended to assess whether relevant source information is represented in a summary without requiring a reference summary. It evaluates consistency and relevance alongside coherence and fluency and is relevant to content-coverage assessment.

title: Evaluating Attribution in Dialogue Systems: The BEGIN Benchmark
abstract: Introduces a human-annotated benchmark for evaluating whether generated dialogue responses are attributable to provided background evidence. It meta-evaluates multiple automatic metrics and finds important failures on abstractive responses and under shifts to longer source documents.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models
abstract: Defines the Attributable to Identified Sources evaluation framework for determining whether externally grounded NLG statements are supported by identified source material. The framework is validated through human evaluation across conversational QA, summarization, and table-to-text generation.

title: QAFactEval: Improved QA-Based Factual Consistency Evaluation for Summarization
abstract: Systematically analyzes components of QA-based factual-consistency metrics and proposes QAFactEval. The work compares entailment and QA approaches against human-annotated factuality benchmarks and shows that the two paradigms can provide complementary signals.

title: Learn then Test: Calibrating Predictive Algorithms to Achieve Risk Control
abstract: Introduces a model-agnostic calibration framework that selects operating parameters so specified risks satisfy finite-sample statistical guarantees. It reframes calibration as a multiple-testing problem and provides a general transfer mechanism for bounded-risk deployment.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Extends conformal prediction from set coverage to control of expected monotone loss functions. The framework includes extensions for distribution shift and demonstrates risk control on both computer-vision and natural-language-processing losses.

title: Revisiting the Gold Standard: Grounding Summarization Evaluation with Robust Human Evaluation
abstract: Introduces Atomic Content Units and the RoSE benchmark to strengthen human evaluation of summarization salience and content coverage. It collects large-scale human annotations, compares evaluation protocols, and meta-evaluates many automatic metrics, exposing confounds and instability in less structured human evaluation.

title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
abstract: Proposes a sampling-based method for detecting factual hallucinations without an external evidence database or access to model probabilities. It evaluates sentence-level factuality and passage-level ranking against human annotations, providing a transfer baseline for uncertainty-based factuality screening.

title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
abstract: Decomposes long-form generations into atomic factual claims and measures the proportion supported by a reliable knowledge source. Human evaluation and automated estimation demonstrate the value of preserving a claim-level factual-precision denominator rather than assigning one undifferentiated score to an entire generation.

title: Improved Online Conformal Prediction via Strongly Adaptive Online Learning
abstract: Develops online conformal methods for environments whose distributions may change arbitrarily over time. Strongly adaptive regret provides guarantees over many subintervals rather than only across the full history, which is directly relevant to continuing non-stationary streams.

title: Conformal PID Control for Time Series Prediction
abstract: Combines conformal prediction with control-theoretic feedback to adapt uncertainty sets in the presence of seasonality, trends, systematic error, and general distribution shifts. Its online adaptation machinery is a transfer candidate for temporally changing calibration problems.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Evaluates retrieval-augmented generation along separate dimensions of context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance using trained lightweight judges and a small amount of human-annotated data. It additionally evaluates robustness when query or document domains change.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: Provides a large human-annotated corpus of naturally generated retrieval-augmented responses with hallucinations marked at fine-grained span level. The annotations distinguish unsupported or contradictory generated content from material grounded in retrieved sources and support meta-evaluation of hallucination detectors.

title: Long-form factuality in large language models
abstract: Introduces LongFact and the Search-Augmented Factuality Evaluator, which decomposes long-form responses into individual factual claims, searches for external evidence, and verifies each claim. It also proposes an F1-style aggregate balancing supported-fact precision with an output-length-based recall component.

title: Merging Facts, Crafting Fallacies: Evaluating the Contradictory Nature of Aggregated Factual Claims in Long-Form Generations
abstract: Shows that independently factual subclaims can combine into an incorrect long-form statement, especially under entity ambiguity. It demonstrates failure cases for atomic-fact metrics and citation recall and proposes D-FActScore to better account for contradictions introduced when claims are aggregated.

title: A Closer Look at Claim Decomposition
abstract: Examines how claim-decomposition choices affect factual-support evaluation and shows that metrics such as FActScore can be sensitive to decomposition errors. It introduces DecompScore and a semantics-inspired decomposition method intended to produce better atomic subclaims.

title: ACUEval: Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation and Correction for Abstractive Summarization
abstract: Proposes a two-stage evaluation strategy that decomposes summaries into atomic content units and validates each unit against the source document. The method is designed to improve interpretability over single-score LLM evaluators and is meta-evaluated against human faithfulness judgments.

title: On the Evaluation of Machine-Generated Reports
abstract: Proposes an evaluation framework for machine-generated long-form reports centered on completeness, accuracy, and verifiability. The framework uses required information nuggets to assess completeness and accuracy and mappings from report claims to source documents to assess citation-based verifiability.

title: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces a claim-level diagnostic framework for evaluating both retrieval and generation in RAG systems. Its metrics separately expose whether ground-truth claims were retrieved, whether retrieved evidence was actually used, and whether generated answers are correct and complete, with meta-evaluation against human preferences.

title: Evaluation of Attribution Bias in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
abstract: Studies whether attribution evaluations in RAG systems are sensitive to source-authorship metadata and whether models systematically prefer human- or AI-authored sources. Counterfactual evaluation demonstrates that source metadata can materially change attribution behavior, identifying an evaluator robustness issue relevant to provenance-sensitive systems.

title: Conformal Prediction for Natural Language Processing: A Survey
abstract: Surveys conformal prediction methods and applications across NLP, including generation and hallucination-risk control. It emphasizes that ordinary conformal assumptions are difficult to satisfy in autoregressive free-form generation and highlights exchangeability and output-structure challenges.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: SemanticCite: Citation Verification with AI-Powered Full-Text Analysis and Evidence-Based Reasoning
abstract: Introduces a citation-verification system that analyzes full source text and labels claim-source relations as Supported, Partially Supported, Unsupported, or Uncertain. The explicit partial-support category is relevant to evaluating evidence sufficiency for compound or only partly substantiated claims.

title: FaStFACT: Faster, Stronger Long-Form Factuality Evaluations in LLMs
abstract: Adapts the decompose-search-verify pipeline for long-form factuality with chunk-level claim extraction, confidence-based pre-verification, and document-level evidence retrieval. The work explicitly targets failures caused by inaccurate claim sets and insufficient evidence collection and validates the evaluator against manual annotations.

title: Beyond Precision: Importance-Aware Recall for Factuality Evaluation in Long-Form LLM Generation
abstract: Argues that factuality evaluation should measure both supported-claim precision and whether generated text covers the relevant facts it ought to contain. It constructs reference facts from external sources and introduces relevance- and salience-aware weighting for factual recall, directly targeting factual incompleteness in long-form generation.

title: When Should LLMs Be Less Specific? Selective Abstraction for Reliable Long-Form Text Generation
abstract: Extends binary abstention to claim-level selective abstraction for long-form generation, allowing uncertain factual atoms to be replaced by less specific statements. Evaluation explicitly couples factual risk with an information-theoretic coverage measure and compares methods using risk-coverage curves.

title: Optimal training-conditional regret for online conformal prediction
abstract: Studies online conformal prediction for non-stationary streams with unknown abrupt or smooth distribution drift. It uses drift detection and training-conditional cumulative regret to obtain adaptation guarantees for both pretrained and online-trained nonconformity scores.

title: Hierarchical Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control for Selective Prediction in Language Models
abstract: Extends conformal risk control for selective prediction in language models to heterogeneous groups structured by domain, topic difficulty, and linguistic style. It addresses the limitation that a marginal risk guarantee can conceal subgroup-specific overexposure to errors.

title: Evaluating LLM Uncertainty in Long-Form Generation Using Deterministic Ground Truth
abstract: Introduces SALT, a deterministic long-form benchmark supporting fine-grained evaluation of correctness, calibration, and confidence ranking without relying on noisy external judges. Experiments across many LLMs show that uncertainty ranking can degrade substantially at atomic resolution and reveal accuracy-calibration tradeoffs from reasoning.

title: Towards Query-Agnostic RAG Evaluation via Query Coverage and Claim Verifiability
abstract: Introduces Q-CARE, which decomposes queries into subqueries and generated answers into atomic claims to evaluate query coverage and claim verifiability. It provides distinct generator metrics for completeness, conciseness, and verifiableness and meta-evaluates them on a human-annotated benchmark spanning multiple datasets.
